research_question: Can a source-header temporal backoff distinguish duration flows from point-in-time balances when a financial question mentions only a bare fiscal year?

hypothesis.observed_phenomenon: Most year-bearing questions use a bare year even when the source table explicitly states a duration or instant reporting convention.
hypothesis.possible_cause: Question-only temporal parsing cannot recover duration versus instant semantics from a bare year.
hypothesis.expected_improvement: Use the source table header only as a backoff when the question itself has no explicit temporal type; this should convert correct source-supported abstentions into correct classifications.
hypothesis.possible_side_effect: A mixed or truncated table header could be misread and create a confident but wrong temporal type.
hypothesis.questions_that_should_improve: Bare-year questions grounded to tables with an explicit Years Ended/Fiscal duration anchor or As Of/At-Date/Balance Sheet instant anchor.
hypothesis.questions_that_should_remain_unchanged: Questions with an explicit temporal type, source headers without exactly one temporal anchor, records contaminated by exp/greater inspection, and questions without a four-digit year.

split_design.company_holdout: FinQA issuer IDs are pairwise disjoint across discovery, development, and untouched.
split_design.wording_holdout: Development and untouched normalized question wording templates are disjoint.
split_design.metric_holdout: At least one metric family has six or more untouched records and zero development records.
split_design.composition_holdout: At least one temporal-label plus program-composition signature has six or more untouched records and zero development records.

contamination_register.reason: Specific exp-related FinQA test examples were inspected before the scalar hypothesis; excluding them also prevents any cross-experiment ambiguity.

evaluator.kind: FinQA source table header with exactly one explicit financial-period anchor
